'''Isezuka Kofun''' (伊勢塚古墳) is an ancient Kofun ([[kofun]]) located in {{ill|Kamiochiai, Fujioka, Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県藤岡市上落合}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shiroishi Kofun Group|ja|白石古墳群}} and is Historic Site1 as a Historic Site by Gunma Prefecture.

== Overview ==
The Isezuka Kofun is situated on the lowest terrace of a three-level river terrace typeed along the right bank of the Kabura River in southern Gunma Prefecture. Multiple archaeological investigations have been conducted at the site.

The mound is an irregular octagon, measuring 27.2 meters in diameter and 6 meters in height{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The mound consists of four tiers, with the lowest tier being polygonal (irregular octagon) and the udder tiers being circular{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The mound’s surface is covered with {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|qid=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}}, and cylindrical, humanoid, and shield-shaped {{ill|Haniwa|ar|هانيوا|ca|Haniwa|cs|Haniwa|de|Haniwa|eo|Haniva|es|Haniwa|fi|Haniwa|fr|Haniwa|hu|Haniva|id|Haniwa|it|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|mk|Ханива|nl|Haniwa|pl|Haniwa|pt|Haniwa|ru|Ханива|sr|Ханива|sv|Haniwa|th|ฮานิวะ|tr|Haniwa|uk|Ханіва|zh|埴轮|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} were found on the second tier{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The burial chamber is a double-sleeved {{ill|yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southward. It is the largest stone chamber in Fujioka City and is notable for its distinctive "pattern masonry" construction and dome-shaped ceiling{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}. burial goods such as {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} have been discovered. The mound is estimated to have been built in the late {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} (late 6th century){{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}} or the latter half of the 6th century<ref name="Description Board">Historic Site description board.</ref>.

The site was Historic Site1 a Gunma Prefecture Historic Site in 1973 (Shōwa 48)<ref name="Gunma Prefecture"/>. It has since been preserved and made accessible to the public.

== burial Chamber ==
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-B-2.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Overview of the stone chamber}}]]
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-N-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber diagram}}]]
The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} that opens southward. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}:
* Total length: 8.9 meters
* burial chamber: Length 4.7 meters, rear wall width 1.84 meters, central width 2.41 meters, front width 1.54 meters
* Passage: Length 4.24 meters

The stone chamber features unique "pattern masonry," where quartzite cobbles and schist slabs are arranged vertically. The chamber has a domed ceiling, and its cross-section is hourglass-shaped<ref name="Description Board"/>. The ceiling stones consist of two rounded sandstone pieces, and the rear wall is similarly made of sandstone{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}. The entry portal is constructed with schist slabs, including a pseudo-lintel{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}.

It is part of the {{ill|Shiroishi Kofun Group|ja|白石古墳群|lt=Shiraishi Kofun Cluster}} and is designated as a {{ill|Gunma Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties|ja|群馬県指定文化財}} (Historic Site).

== Overview ==
Situated on the lowest terrace of a three-tier riverbank along the right bank of the {{ill|Kabura River|ja|鏑川}}, this tumulus has undergone several excavations. Initially thought to be a circular mound, investigations confirmed its irregular octagonal shape. The mound measures 27.2 meters in diameter and 6 meters in height, with a four-tier structure: the lowest tier is polygonal (irregular octagonal), and the remaining tiers are circular.

The surface of the mound is covered with stone lining ({{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|qid=Q11621213|lt=Fukiishi}}), and artifacts such as {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪}}, human-shaped haniwa, and shield-shaped haniwa were unearthed from the second tier. The burial chamber, which opens southward, is a double-shouldered {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}. Known for its distinctive "patterned masonry" and domed ceiling, this stone chamber is the largest in Fujioka.

The construction period is estimated to be the late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|qid=Q8090|lt=6th century}} or possibly the latter half of the 6th century. The site was designated a Gunma Prefectural Historic Site in 1973 and is currently open to the public after restoration.

== Burial Chamber ==
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-B-2.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Overhead view of the stone chamber}}]]
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-N-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Layout of the stone chamber}}]]
The burial chamber consists of a double-shouldered {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southward. area are as follows:
* Total length: 8.9 meters
* Main chamber: Length 4.7 m; width at rear wall: 1.84 m; central width: 2.41 m; front width: 1.54 m
* Passage: Length 4.24 m

The chamber is constructed with a unique "patterned masonry" technique, using primarily siliceous stones with elongated schist slabs stacked edge-on. The domed ceiling is achieved by angling the sidewalls inward. The rear wall and ceiling stones are made of sandstone, and the main entrance features green schist slabs, including a pseudo-lintel. The passage uses pillar-shaped cut sandstone.

'''Isezuka Kofun''' (伊勢塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} (tumulus) located in {{ill|Fujioka, Gunma|ar|فوجيوكا (غونما)|azb|فوجی‌اوکا، قونما|ce|Фудзиока (гӀала, Гумма)|ceb|Fujioka (lungsod sa Hapon, Gunma-ken)|de|Fujioka (Gunma)|eo|Fuĵioka|es|Fujioka|fa|فوجی‌اوکا، گونما|fi|Fujioka|fr|Fujioka|gl|Fujioka, Gunma|hu|Fudzsioka (Gunma)|id|Fujioka, Gunma|it|Fujioka|ja|藤岡市|ko|후지오카시|mg|Fujioka|mzn|فوجی‌اوکا، گونما|nl|Fujioka (Gunma)|pl|Fujioka|pt|Fujioka|ro|Fujioka|ru|Фудзиока (город, Гумма)|sr|Фуџиока|sv|Fujioka, Gunma|tg|Фуҷиока|tl|Fujioka, Gunma|tr|Fujioka|tt|Фудзиока (шәһәр, Гумма)|uk|Фудзіока (Ґумма)|ur|فوجیوکا، گنما|uz|Fujioka (Gunma)|vi|Fujioka, Gunma|war|Fujioka, Gunma|zh|藤岡市|zh_classical|藤岡市|zh_min_nan|Huzioka-chhī|zh_yue|藤岡|qid=Q596486|lt=Fujioka, Gunma}}, Gunma Prefecture. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳}} and part of the {{ill|Shiroishi Kofun Group|ja|白石古墳群}}. The tumulus has been designated as a Gunma Prefecture Historic Site.

== Overview ==
The tumulus was constructed on the lowest terrace of a three-tiered river terrace formed by the Kaburagawa River in southern Gunma Prefecture. Multiple archaeological investigations have been conducted.

The mound is an irregular octagon, measuring 27.2 meters in diameter and 6 meters in height.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}</ref> The mound consists of four tiers, with only the lowest tier having a polygonal shape, while the upper tiers are circular.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}</ref> The mound features {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|qid=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}}, and cylindrical and figurative {{ill|Haniwa|ar|هانيوا|ca|Haniwa|cs|Haniwa|de|Haniwa|eo|Haniva|es|Haniwa|fi|Haniwa|fr|Haniwa|hu|Haniva|id|Haniwa|it|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|mk|Ханива|nl|Haniwa|pl|Haniwa|pt|Haniwa|ru|Ханива|sr|Ханива|sv|Haniwa|th|ฮานิวะ|tr|Haniwa|uk|Ханіва|zh|埴轮|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} (human-shaped, shield-shaped) were discovered on the second tier.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}</ref> 

The burial facility is a dual-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} oriented to the south. The chamber is the largest in Fujioka City, notable for its "patterned masonry" style, characterized by alternating use of rounded tuff stones and slender schist blocks. The chamber is further distinguished by its domed ceiling.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}</ref> The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}</ref>

The tumulus was designated a Gunma Prefecture Historic Site in 1973.<ref name="群馬県">{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.gunma.jp/contents/100155734.pdf 群馬県内の県指定文化財一覧]}}（群馬県ホームページ）。</ref> It is now maintained as part of a public park.

== Burial Structure ==
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-B-2.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Overhead view of the stone chamber}}]]
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-N-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber layout}}]]
The burial structure is a dual-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}. The chamber's specifications are as follows:<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}</ref>
* Total length: 8.9 m
* Main chamber: Length 4.7 m, rear width 1.84 m, middlewidth 2.41 m, entrance width 1.54 m
* Passageway: Length 4.24 m

The chamber employs "patterned masonry," where round tuff stones alternate with schist blocks.<ref>{{Harv|伊勢塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}</ref> The domed ceiling is achieved by corbelling the walls inward. The entrance features sandstone lintels and imitation doorways.
